title: II-VI: Gods virtue; wisdom and prudence
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Jeremiah 10:12. By this God decrees plus does all things out from ye most wise counsel belonging toward His will — Isaiah 40:28; Prudence stands as integrity belonging toward intellect by means belonging toward that same which God knows how to accommodate to all things in order to practice what stands as fitting. VI. 1 John 3:20. Hebrews 4:13; 1 Timothy 1:17; Romans 11:33; Psalm 139; 1 Samuel 2:3; future, existing in act, past — Job 11; — by this God most inwardly knows Himself plus all things — possible. Wisdom stands as integrity belonging toward intellect by means belonging toward that same which God knows what agrees with each thing plus what stands as alien out from it. V. Integrity belonging toward intellect stands as wisdom plus prudence. IV. For He Himself stands as to Himself ye right reason belonging toward all things knowable plus to be done. plus therefore not a quality or habit belonging toward intellect plus will, but Gods very essence considered in order to ye true plus ye good, plus a certain eminence belonging toward that same that which in our virtues plus affections stands as most perfect — virtue in God stands as not an accident. Gods virtue stands as ye integrity belonging toward His intellect or will. III. But Gods stand as virtue plus blessedness. II.
pass_b_english: II. But Gods are virtue and blessedness. III. Gods virtue is the integrity of His intellect or will. Virtue in God is not an accident, and therefore not a quality or habit of intellect and will, but Gods very essence considered in order to the true and the good, and a certain eminence of that which in our virtues and affections is most perfect. For He Himself is to Himself the right reason of all things knowable and to be done.

IV. Integrity of intellect is wisdom and prudence. V. Wisdom is integrity of intellect by which God knows what agrees with each thing and what is alien from it. By this God most inwardly knows Himself and all things — possible, future, existing in act, past — Job 11; 1 Samuel 2:3; Psalm 139; Romans 11:33; 1 Timothy 1:17; Hebrews 4:13; 1 John 3:20.

VI. Prudence is integrity of intellect by which God knows how to accommodate to all things in order to practice what is fitting. By this God decrees and does all things from the most wise counsel of His will — Isaiah 40:28; Jeremiah 10:12.
source_text: II. Sunt autem Dei virtus et beatitas. III. Virtus Dei est integritas intellectus ejus aut voluntatis. Virtus in Deo non est accidens, adeoque qualitas seu habitus intellectus et voluntatis, sed ipsissima Dei essentia considerata in ordine ad verum et bonum, et eminentia quaedam ejus quod in virtutibus et affectibus nostris perfectissimum est. Ipse enim sibi est ratio recta omnium scibilium et faciendorum. IV. Integritas intellectus est sapientia et prudentia. V. Sapientia est integritas intellectus, qua Deus novit quid cuique rei conveniat et quid ab ipsa sit alienum. Hac Deus intime novit se et res omnes, possibiles, futuras, existentes actu, praeteritas — Job XI; I Sam. II.3; Psal. CXXXIX; Rom. XI.33; I Tim. I.17; Heb. IV.13; I Joh. III.20. VI. Prudentia est integritas intellectus, qua Deus novit rebus omnibus in ordine ad praxin accommodare quod convenit. Hac Deus omnia decernit et facit ex sapientissimo consilio voluntatis suae — Isa. XL.28; Jer. X.12.
